title: Knowledge check: Webhook Authentication and Reliability

questions.prompt: What makes a webhook receiver reliable?
options: Parse and mutate business state before signature verification.
Assume providers never retry and events always arrive in order.
Verify the provider signature over the correct request bytes and deduplicate event IDs before applying side effects.
Trust the source IP alone and process every delivery exactly once by assumption.
questions.answer_key: Verify the provider signature over the correct request bytes and deduplicate event IDs before applying side effects.
questions.explanation: Verify the provider signature over the correct request bytes and deduplicate event IDs before applying side effects. This is especially relevant to “Webhook Authentication and Reliability” because the API contract must remain explicit and reviewable.

questions.prompt: For the lesson “Webhook Authentication and Reliability”, which check provides the strongest practical evidence?
options: Test against production records so the exercise cannot be repeated safely.
Test valid, invalid, replayed, duplicate, and out-of-order webhook deliveries.
Rely on a code review comment without running any representative check.
Run one happy-path call and skip invalid, denied, and failure scenarios.
questions.answer_key: Test valid, invalid, replayed, duplicate, and out-of-order webhook deliveries.
questions.explanation: A useful check is repeatable, tied to an observable contract, and includes an important negative or boundary scenario.

questions.prompt: Which review warning is most relevant to “Webhook Authentication and Reliability”?
options: Webhook side effects occur before verification or every retry is processed as new.
The expected behavior and relevant failure cases are documented.
A representative test can reproduce the result.
The API avoids exposing internal secrets and personal data.
questions.answer_key: Webhook side effects occur before verification or every retry is processed as new.
questions.explanation: This finding weakens a core API guarantee and should be treated as a design or release issue, not only a style concern.
